painpoints: `.fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/implementer.md:22` tells the gate-red bounce to read `output.gate_known_bug_hits` from `## Context`, but the graph produces and declares `output.gatebounce` (`.fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro:332` producer, `:266` implementer read list) — the prompt names a key that can never arrive, so the known-bug-matching instruction is dead on arrival; same class as the earlier `output.gatebounce` key-mismatch painpoint in this lane. Evidence: run `petri` (implementer.md:22 vs workflow.fabro:266/332). Fix: rename the prompt key to `output.gatebounce` (the engine derives the key from node id `gatebounce`), or align the producer back.

The develop implementer node sets BOTH `x.context_allow_keys` (`.fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro:292`) and `x.preamble_allow_keys` (`:266`) with disjoint sets, and petri's `context_visible` intersects the two lists (pinned rev 13e4e66), so the implementer's `## Context` rendered EMPTY: in run `petri` my implementer prompt carried no `## Context` section at all, and I recovered the claimed seed id from the claim_check stage output instead of "reading it there FIRST" as the prompt instructs; the seed trio is additionally blocked by `is_hidden_key`'s `current*` arm. Fix: declare read keys on both lists AND move seed keys off the `current*` prefix, or rewrite the Input contract to point at the claim_check output — needs a seed.
observations: A delta key's read path is the INTERSECTION of `x.context_allow_keys` and `x.preamble_allow_keys` (petri `fork_preamble_policy::context_visible`): any future key for a direct re-entry edge must ride BOTH lists or it renders nothing — hence `review_feedback` declared twice in `.fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro:266,292`.

The develop reviewer's label contract is the built-in `output_schema="routing"` (`.fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro:460`), which restricts `preferred_next_label` to the node's outgoing edge labels dynamically — no schema file or `workflow.toml` enumerates reviewer labels, so a new label needs no schema edit (verified: zero `Changes requested` matches under `.fabro/workflows/develop/schemas/` and `.fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.toml`).

`.fabro/workflows/loop/workflow.fabro:244` still routes the loop's own reviewer only through its planner — this seed scoped the develop unit only, so the loop unit's direct edge remains a separate one-unit candidate for a future seed.
